newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds rise in line with Europe on U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds rise in line with Europe on U.S. data.

text.p: Irish bonds rose in thin late trade on Friday in line with European debt markets after the release of U.S. data but the domestic market also kept a close eye on the Irish pound, dealers said.

"The focus at home is on the currencies with the Irish pound very high on the ERM grid. All eyes are on the Irish Central Bank to see what they will do. It will be interesting to see will they intervene or what will they do?" one dealer said.
Dealers said a slightly stronger than expected rise in U.S. non-farm payrolls in January was offset by a fall in hours worked and a rise in the unemployment rate.
The data indicated strong growth in U.S. job creation without excessive inflationary pressure, dealers said.
Payrolls rose 271,000 in January versus forecasts of a 237,000 rise. Average weekly hours fell to 34.1 from 34.8 in December and average hourly earnings rose only once cent to $12.06.

By 1600 GMT, the 6.5 percent bond due 2001 was up 25 pence from Thursday's close at 103.05 to yield 5.73 percent while the key benchmark eight percent bond was up 30 pence from the close at 110.45 to yield 6.48 percent.
Dealers said Irish bonds were trading at 90 basis points over German bunds in the 10-year area and 153 basis points over bunds in the five-year area.
